Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: do_kill()/do_waitpid() match free pcb slots when pid == -1, then walk an uninitialised wait_list
FILE: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c
CLAIM: Both lookups (lines 343-348 and 392-397) accept `pcb[i].pid == pid` without excluding the free-slot sentinel -1. A never-used slot lives in BSS, so status == 0 == TASK_BLOCKED and wait_list == {NULL, NULL} (only init_pcb() and do_exec() run init_list_head on it).

Concrete failure: any user program calling sys_kill(-1) (or `kill /` in the shell, since tiny_libc atoi maps '/' to -1) selects the first free slot, passes the TASK_EXITED/ZOMBIE/KILLED guard, and enters release_resources(). `list_empty(&task->wait_list)` evaluates NULL == &wait_list -> false, so it calls do_unblock(NULL) -> list_del(NULL) dereferences address 8 in S-mode. handle_page_fault (kernel/mm/mm.c:395) sees stval < the user limit and maps a _PAGE_USER page at VA 0 in the current pgdir; with SUM clear the retried kernel load faults again, giving an unbreakable page-fault loop that wedges the hart with the global kernel lock held. sys_waitpid(-1) reaches the same uninitialised head through do_block()/list_add_tail (`head->prev` is NULL -> NULL->next store).

I could not refute the claim — every premise checks out against the real files.

**Verification chain:**

1. **Free slots really are `pid == -1` with a raw-BSS `wait_list`.** `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/init/main.c:94-96` does only `for(int i = 0; i < NUM_MAX_TASK; i++){ pcb[i].pid = -1; }`. `init_list_head(&pcb[0].wait_list)` (line 105) is the *only* wait_list init at boot; slots 1..N-1 keep `{NULL, NULL}` from BSS. `init_list_head(&new_pcb->wait_list)` in the new code (`sched.c:226`) only runs once a slot is actually allocated by `do_exec`.

2. **`TASK_BLOCKED == 0`** — it's the first enumerator in `include/os/sched.h:56`, so a pristine slot's `status` (BSS zero) passes the `EXITED/ZOMBIE/KILLED` guard in `do_kill` unchanged.

3. **The lookups are new code and have no sentinel filter.** `git diff` confirms both `if (pcb[i].pid == pid)` lines are additions (`kernel/sched/sched.c:337` in `do_kill`, `:392` in `do_waitpid`). Ironically `do_waitpid` itself *writes* the sentinel (`child->pid = -1;` at line 410), and `alloc_pcb` reads it (`sched.c:199-202`: "`pid == -1` marks an unused slot") — so the new code establishes the sentinel and then matches on it.

4. **`release_resources` is worse than a single deref — it's an unbounded loop.** `sched.c:275-277`:
   ```c
   while (!list_empty(&task->wait_list)) {
       do_unblock(task->wait_list.next);
   }
   ```
   `list_empty` is `head->next == head` (`list.h:106`), so `NULL == &wait_list` is false → `do_unblock(NULL)`. `do_unblock` never touches `task->wait_list`, so even if the deref survived, the loop condition never changes: infinite loop with `preempt_count` raised and the global kernel lock held.

5. **`do_unblock(NULL)` faults.** `list_del(NULL)` reads `entry->prev`; `struct list_node { next, prev; }` (`list.h:42-45`) puts `prev` at offset 8, so it's a load from VA 8 — exactly as claimed. Then `list_add_tail(NULL, &ready_queue)` → `_list_add(NULL, ready_queue.prev, &ready_queue)` stores `node->next` at VA 0.

6. **The fault handler makes it unrecoverable rather than fatal.** `kernel/mm/mm.c:395-406` only escalates to `handle_other` when `stval >= (1lu << (VPN2_SHIFT + PPN_BITS - 1))`; `stval == 8` is below that, so it calls `alloc_page_helper(8, current pgdir)` and retries — a kernel-mode access to a `_PAGE_USER` page, plus the loop from point 4 either way.

7. **Reachable from the stock shell.** `tiny_libc/string.c:80-88` `atoi` has no sign/digit handling: `atoi("/") = '/' - '0' = -1`. `test/test_shell.c:335-345` only rejects `pid == 0 || pid == 1` before calling `sys_kill(pid)`. `sys_kill` passes `(long)pid` (`tiny_libc/syscall.c:19-22`), `handle_syscall` forwards `regs[10]` untouched (`kernel/syscall/syscall.c:9`), and `init/main.c:134-135` wires `do_kill`/`do_waitpid` directly with no wrapper. So typing `kill /` in the shell wedges the hart.

The only inaccuracies are cosmetic: the claim cites lines 343-348 / 392-397 (actual: 336-342 / 391-397), and the primary symptom is the non-terminating `while` in `release_resources` rather than a one-shot deref. Neither weakens the finding.

Relevant files: `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/init/main.c`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/list.h`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/include/os/sched.h`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/mm/mm.c`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/tiny_libc/string.c`, `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/test/test_shell.c`.
